source: Verona, for a while I take my leave, to see my friends in Padua.
(Oh. The play's just starting.)
Watch the performance?

source: But of all—my best beloved and approved friend, Hortensio; and I trow this is his house.
(Katherine's onstage. I won't disturb her this time.)
Good morrow, Kate! For that's your name, I hear.
Hmm. Well have you heard, but something hard of hearing. They call me Katharine that do talk of me.
(Katherine looks so familiar. Who is she?)
(I feel as if I know that voice.)
(She looks happy.)
...Husband, let's follow to see the end of this ado.
First kiss me, Kate, and we will.
W-what, in the midst of the street?
What, art thou ashamed of me?
No, sir, God forbid, but ashamed to kiss.
Why, then, let's home again.
Nay, I will give thee a kiss!
Now pray thee, love, stay.
Is not this well? Come, my sweet Kate! Better once than never, for never too late!
Is... is that you?
What are you doing here?
Oy! Kate! You've lost yer nerve!
What's goin' on?
I paid for this!
C'mon! Say something!
Wait! Don't go—
I shouldn't have done that.
But I never knew.
She went to the bar.
Something stiff, Othello. Please.
Oh, so you're drinking again?
Saw you out there earlier tonight. That's some good delivery.
Looked like you had the crowd in a vise.
Is... that... really you?
How can you be outside the castle?
And how long did it take you to recognize me?
Never mind that. Look, I came because I was worried about you. You ran off so quickly.
Well, there's no point pretending now.
What you saw on stage... is me. Or the 'rest' of me, I suppose.
For many years, I've been a player. It started when I was a child, playing Juliet.
And tonight... it ended, as Katherine.
Why must it end?
For a boy player, there are only two options when one grows old: Take the male parts, or leave the stage.
And I would rather leave.
I never thought the day would come when I would have to stop. I never wanted to.
In the moments when I was up there... I felt... like I was showing the world the truer form of myself.
The 'me' who was not just strong, but beautiful.
You and that Petruchio actor...
It was stageplay, Ophelia.
Very convincing stageplay.
My lady, please. I don't want to... I can't think about all of this right now.
In my life at the castle, I spend every shred of my willpower trying not to think about it.
Does anyone in Elsinore know?
Only Claudius. He used it to keep me in fear.
A-and you now know, I suppose. I've used a pseudonym these long years, kept my face hidden when I left the changing room.
My father found out. Hated me for it. But he's dead now, and took his shame with him, and told no one.
Right before he died, he told me the world would turn on me if they ever knew.
Well, he was wrong about that. About me, at least.
You can trust me. How many years have we known each other? You've always taken care of me. Now it's my turn.
Hamlet... you could trust in him, too, I think.
Hamlet? No. I think not.
There are others you could trust in, too, I think.
No. No, certainly not.
What if word got out, Ophelia? Think! Would I be Guard Captain still? Or would they snicker and taunt just as they did tonight, right to my face?
Or worse, would they try to destroy me?
I pray to God daily, but I don't know that He listens to me anymore.
Bernardo—Katherine—whomever you desire to be...
My father has a saying for times like this. 'To thine own self be true.'
If this is your truth, then God will love you for it.
What you choose to tell others is up to you. But I will always—always be your friend.
There's that, at least.
How should I call you?
By which I mean, how would you like to be called?
Call me Bernardo. Man or woman, I know not which. Some days one, then the other. Both are to my liking.
It would be easier for now if you called me as a man before my own men. Some of them... would... react poorly to who I am, I suspect.
If that's your wish, I'll honor it.
Will you not speak to Hamlet and my brother? They've known you since you were a child, after all.
Will you not speak to any others whom you trust?
They might fear me. Hate me. Pity me.
I can trust no one with this. Not right now, not when I'm in the position I am, and when the country's at war.
I've felt so alone for so long.
I must return to the castle soon. But for now, I'll linger a while.
Please be careful in town. Were I in my right mind I'd escort you home, but I hope you'll forgive me for sending you alone.
M-my prince Fortinbras!
I didn't believe you'd come in person. A-and without guard. Is it safe?
Safe enough through the woods. Our father cared mightily about royal appearances in war. We rather prefer victory.
Lady Brockenhuus. You look well. And your father?
As well as ever, my lord.
What news can you deliver?
The King believes your peace offering is legitimate. He wishes to pursue an end to the present squabble.
He will offer you and your men safe passage through Denmark.
What a fool. He is his brother's lesser, to be certain.
The King is suspicious of you. I observed his War Council meeting in private. But he's not yet suspicious enough to act against you.
Be cautious, my lord.
I suspect it shall take the old man far longer to act against me than I against him.
The King is dead.
For the time being, you're free to act as you please. The castle is in chaos.
Well, then. This certainly a pleasant surprise.
This is wonderful news. Were my father alive to see how our mobilization has succeeded, he'd certainly be proud.
...And when I am King of Denmark, your family will be justly rewarded for your show of faith.
T-thank you, sire.
Keep your ears to the earth. I'll see you tomorrow night.
(...Brit's the spy plaguing Elsinore? Her?)
(It can't be possible... can it?)
(Bernardo and the King must know about this. Immediately.)
I... I've further news for you, my lord Fortinbras.
Excellent. My time is increasingly limited as we prepare for the siege.
Claudius's efforts are regaining focus. I'm... concerned. His throne may need to be melted at the base, so to speak.
The people are starving and unhappy under Claudius's ill-fitted rule. All they need is an excuse to storm the castle.
If there were someone who could lead a siege, better if it was a Dane... perhaps the prince?
No. He's far too indecisive in his own right.
There is another. A Duke's son. He has the love of the people. He would be amenable to your rule.
But... Laertes has sailed for Paris. He's not within Denmark at the moment.
What would cause him to return, furious and full of righteous fire?
What would cause him to take action against the king, furious and full of righteous fire?
...I don't know.
No. Wait. He has a sister.
A delicate little thing, hardly grown. If something were to happen to her—he'd get his revenge in an instant.
He loves her more than anything in this world.
Claudius is dead, as well I'm sure you've heard by now.
And Hamlet is to succeed him.
I believe my father has sent his recommendation that Hamlet and I be betrothed. What would you have me do, my lord?
You know that I have indomitable faith in the way you think and act. If young Hamlet is King, then you must stand by his side.
After my men have settled the castle and flown the flag of Norway, he will need someone to steer him under my interests.
So you aim to make him a puppet.
Yes. A King in name, but a vassal to me in spirit.
I fear there's something impossible in that. He would reject a betrothal at the moment, I think.
Even though Hamlet agreed to the betrothal, I fear any attempt to use it to sway him would fail.
His heart belongs to someone else.
To whom?
The daughter of Duke Polonius. Her name is Ophelia. And she is a strong-headed girl. She cannot be easily persuaded.
So long as Ophelia lives, Hamlet will never be fully faithful to any bride he's given.
I see. Then the path forward is clear.
Are you prepared to eliminate her of your own hand?
You know her face, her habits, her comings and goings. My men and I are utterly at your liberty.
...You want me to kill her?
I know it is no easy request. The taking of a life should never be treated lightly.
But... for the good of your country, and for the sake of your father, are you willing?
Your people will no longer starve. Your King will no longer be a cruel despot. I promise you kindness and prosperity.
I... I don't think I can.
Something doesn't feel right about it. I've never liked the girl, but evidently there's something very wrong here.
I don't know if I could kill her.
Very well. I understand.
I will find some other path forward. Worry not. Everything proceeds as it was planned.
Let us meet tomorrow night—in town, not here. I shall have further information on keeping you and your family safe.
I'll do what I can.
I must prepare.
You're doing a magnificent thing, Lady Birgitta. You mustn't forget it.
Let us meet tomorrow night. I shall have further logistical information for your father then.
Explain yourself.
It's a nice evening for a walk?
It's freezing down here.
I like looking at all the ships?
Harbor's empty.
I wanted to see what you were up to?
Mmm hm. There it is.
Good night.
Oh. 'Feely. You gave me a fright.
What brings you down here?
I like to leave the castle when I can.
Call it a break, of sorts.
As you well know, Gertrude seems to frown on courtly women going to town too often. So I come here instead.
Oh, yes. I know all about that.
What of you? It's three in the morning. Oughtn't you to be in bed?
Or are you planning to sneak into Hamlet's?
...Never mind. I don't particularly care. Good night.
It all comes back to where I began.
From the first time I died...
I suspected—perhaps—that this was how things were meant to be.
I've seen so many terrible things. The world tearing itself apart. And all for nothing.
It's all useless.
Perhaps the only good outcome is to do nothing, and see where that fate might lead.
Where... am I?
What just happened?
You've arrived!
What's... everyone... doing here?
Um, you mean you don't know? The show's nearly over!
We're here for the final act, of sorts.
We all came here to see what you'd do next.
